newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt not troubled by Dassault probe.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt not troubled by Dassault probe.

text.p: The Belgian government is not troubled by a court investigation into bribes that allegedly were paid by French aviation group Dassault to the Parti Socialiste (PS), one of the four partners in the centre-left coalition.
"The government is not troubled by this investigation. It does not concern any government member, it is an internal problem of the PS," Dehaene's spokeswoman told Reuters on Tuesday.

Earlier today, the Belgian franc weakened slightly after news that police had raided the PS headquarters. The raid followed the arrest last week of two former PS officials in connection with the Dassault probe.
Laywers of the two officials said on Monday Dassault had paid 30 million Belgian francs to the PS in 1989, in exchange for support in getting an army contract. Dassault has denied all wrongdoing.

"The government is working on the completion of its government agreement, with the reduction of the state deficit to three precent of GDP and the reform of the justice system as top priorities," Dehaene's spokeswoman said.
Asked about opposition parties' calls for elections, she said: "This government has a four-year mandate which ends at the end of 1999. Elections are not on the agenda."
"It is up to the courts now to bring clarity in this (Dassault) case, the sooner the better," she added.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
